messages.content:
<role>
You check one property (signal) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is this a problem with Keelwater's product that a squad could act on? Pass means yes.
Fail if the cause is outside the product (pricing, contracts, the customer's own IT, staffing), if a help article would have answered it, or if it is praise.
A feature request or a described workaround is signal.
The evidence is the title, the problem statement and up to 12 customer quotes with route and date.
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "title": "Handlers tied up on phone calls",
 "problem_statement": "Handlers spend hours daily on phone calls instead of processing claims or managing reserves. This delays claim resolution and reduces efficiency in core tasks.",
 "quotes": [
  {
   "quote": "Every single day. We’ve got handlers spending hours on the phone instead of processing claims or managing reserves.",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-14T16:28:00Z"
  }
 ]
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "The single quote (sales, 2026-10-14) describes handlers spending hours on phone calls instead of processing claims, but neither the problem statement nor the quote identifies any Keelwater product behavior causing or failing to support this. There is no described workaround, feature gap, or product defect—just a general efficiency complaint that could stem from staffing, process, or the customer's own operations. Without a product-linked cause a squad could act on, this is not actionable product signal.", "verdict": "fail"}
